'''Katharine Ellen Sykes''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|OBE|FInstP|CPhys}} (born 20 December 1966)<ref name=whoswho/> is a British [[physicist]], [[Television presenter|broadcaster]]<ref name=imdb>{{IMDb name|nm1391881}}</ref> and [[Professor]] of Sciences and Society at the [[University of Bristol]]. She was previously Collier Professor of [[Public engagement|Public Engagement]] in Science and Engineering, from 2002 to 2006.<ref name=bbc1>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/gloucestershire/8083554.stm|title=BBC NEWS - UK - England - Gloucestershire - Honorary doctorate for professor|access-date=24 January 2017}}</ref> She has presented various [[BBC2]] and [[Open University]] TV series, including ''[[Rough Science]]'', ''Ever Wondered about Food'', ''Alternative Therapies''. ''Alternative Medicine'' and presented for the [[documentary television]] [[miniseries]] ''[[Brave New World with Stephen Hawking]]'' in 2011.<ref name="scopus">{{Scopus|id=7004594748}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1126/science.1151332| pmid = 18048655| title = The Quality of Public Dialogue| journal = Science| volume = 318| issue = 5855| pages = 1349| year = 2007| last1 = Sykes | first1 = K.| doi-access = free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book | doi = 10.1002/9781118551424.ch5| chapter = Responsible Innovation - Opening Up Dialogue and Debate| title = Responsible Innovation| pages = 85| year = 2013| last1 = Sykes | first1 = K. | last2 = MacNaghten | first2 = P. | isbn = 9781118551424}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal

==Education==
Sykes was educated at [[Fitzharrys School]], a co-educational comprehensive school in [[Abingdon, Oxfordshire|Abingdon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/uk/article391121.ece|title=Login|access-date=24 January 2017}}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> She went on to study at the [[University of Bristol]] where she was awarded a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[Physics]] in 1989<ref name="whoswho"/> and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1996 for work on the [[crystallization]] and degradation of [[polyhydroxybutyrate]], a [[biodegradable]] plastic.<ref name="phd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Katharine Ellen|last=Sykes|title=Crystallization and degradation of a biodegradable plastic - polyhydroxybutyrate|publisher=University of Bristol|date=1996 |id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.336867}}|oclc=556686366}}</ref>

==Career==
Sykes helped to create and co-directs [[Cheltenham Science Festival]] and [[Famelab]], a national UK competition which talent spots and trains new faces in science communication. She was Head of Science for [[At-Bristol|Explore-At-Bristol]], in charge of the team creating the content for the award-winning Hands-on Science Centre. She is a member of the [[Council for Science and Technology]] (CST), the UK government's top-level advisory body on science and technology policy issues. She has also served on advisory panels in public engagement in science for the [[Royal Society]], the [[Wellcome Trust]] and [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] (EPSRC). She is a trustee of [[NESTA]]<ref>[http://www.nesta.org.uk/professor-kathy-sykes/ Professor Kathy Sykes] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090417061706/http://www.nesta.org.uk/professor-kathy-sykes/ |date=17 April 2009 }} NESTA</ref> and a board member of [[At-Bristol|Explore-At-Bristol]].

===Awards and honours===
Sykes won the [[Kohn Award]] in 2006 for excellence in engaging the public with science.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/bristol/somerset/5333710.stm|title=Professor wins top science award|website=bbc.co.uk|date=11 September 2006|access-date=24 November 2017}}</ref>  She holds an honorary [[Doctor of Science]] degree and honorary fellowship from the [[University of Gloucestershire]]<ref name=bbc1/><ref>[[Gloucestershire Echo]], 5 June 2009, p. 2</ref> and won the [[Suffrage Science award]] in 2013.

Sykes was appointed [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2009 Birthday Honours]].
